bands.1:
Mirage Mangroves is full of fog. The trees stand on long roots in the water.

"The air is 98 per cent water," says Tully. "My hair is now a bush."

A fat Plonkett frog sits on the anchor. Plonk, plonk, plonk.

Mo makes a mud cake. "With real mud!" he says.

"What did the tree say to the fog?" asks Mo. "I mist you!"

Everyone groans.

A woman paddles out of the fog in a bathtub. Her raincoat is covered in poems. A fluffy grey bird sits on her head.

"Strangers," she says. "Your boat is a soggy sandwich, and you are the filling."

"Is that rude?" whispers Zed.

"It's a metaphor," says Indi.

"Picture it," says the woman. "I am Poet Pip. This is Similoon. Be careful what you compare her to."

"Your bird is as round as a ball," says Mo.

Pop! The Similoon puffs up into a fluffy ball.

Pip tells you about Maxx's video, "Maxx Braves the Wild Mangroves!" In it, he wades through a dark, scary swamp.

"His swamp is a painting," says Pip. "His fog is a liar."

Indi gets it first. "The swamp in his video isn't real!"

Through the fog is a giant green wall, as tall as a house. Gold pipes on top puff out fog. A sign says, "GREEN SCREEN SWAMP. 100% REAL SWAMP."

Frogs sit on the pipes. "He won't like that," says Wren. "He's scared of frogs."

"Will you help us?" you ask.

"Trust is a seed, Captain," says Pip. "It grows slowly. Win my badge."

Then the Similoon flies off to look at the wall.

A voice comes out of the fog. It is Maxx.

"A bird that turns into anything? That's Maxx-imum content! Bag it!"

A net swishes. The Similoon does not come back.

For the first time, Pip speaks plainly. "They took my bird."
bands.2:
Mirage Mangroves is wrapped in fog as thick as porridge. The trees stand in brown water on long roots, like giants paddling in a pond. Somewhere in the mist, something goes plonk.

"The air here is 98 per cent water," says Tully. "And my hair is now 100 per cent bush."

A log turns out to be a white Humbret, standing on one leg and saying sorry to the mud. A fat Plonkett frog sits on the anchor going plonk, plonk, plonk.

Mo serves a chocolate mud cake. "Made with real mud," he says proudly.

Nobody eats it.

"What did the mangrove say to the fog?" asks Mo. "I mist you!"

Everyone groans. Even the Plonkett groans.

A tin bathtub glides out of the fog. A small woman is paddling it with a broom. She has round, foggy glasses and a yellow raincoat covered in handwritten poems. A fluffy grey bird with a long neck sits on her head.

"Strangers," she says. "Your boat is a soggy sandwich, and you are the filling."

"Was that rude?" whispers Zed.

"It's a metaphor," says Indi.

"Picture it," says the woman. "I am Poet Pip. This is Similoon. Be careful what you compare her to."

"Your bird is as round as a ball," says Mo.

Pop! The Similoon puffs into a perfect fluffy ball and rolls into the water.

Pip tells you about Maxx's newest video, "Maxx Braves the Wild Mangroves!" In it, Maxx wades through a dark, dangerous swamp to rescue a Likkaby.

"His swamp is a painting," says Pip. "His fog is a liar."

Everyone looks confused, except Indi. "She means the swamp in his video isn't real!"

"Picture it," says Pip, and she points.

Through a gap in the fog stands a glowing green wall, as tall as a house. Gold pipes along the top puff out clouds of fog. A sign says, "GREEN SCREEN SWAMP. 100% REAL WILD SWAMP."

Plonketts are sitting all over the pipes.

"He won't like that," says Wren. "He's scared of frogs."

"Will you help us?" you ask.

"Trust is a seed, Captain," says Pip. "It grows slowly. Win my badge, and we shall see what blooms."

Just then, the Similoon flutters off towards the green glow to take a look.

A voice drifts out of the fog. It's Maxx, talking to a camera.

"A bird that turns into anything? That's Maxx-imum content, Vantafam! Bag it!"

A net swishes. The Similoon doesn't come back.

For the first time, Poet Pip speaks plainly. "They took my bird."

"What did the mangrove say to the fog?" asks Mo. "I mist you!"

The groan is so loud that even the Plonkett groans.

"Picture it," says the woman. "I am Poet Pip. This is Similoon. Be careful what you compare her to."

"Your bird is as round as a ball," says Mo.

Just then, the Similoon flutters off Pip's head and drifts towards the green glow, curious.

A voice floats out of the fog. It's Maxx, talking to a camera even though it's dark.

"A bird that turns into anything? That's Maxx-imum content, Vantafam! Bag it!"

A net swishes. The Similoon doesn't come back.

"They took my bird."
bands.4:
Mirage Mangroves is wrapped in a fog so thick that you could spread it on toast. The Soggy Biscuit noses between the trees, whose roots rise out of the brown water like the knobbly knees of a thousand giants paddling in a pond. Somewhere in the mist, something goes plonk.

"Statistically," says Tully, "the air here is 98 per cent water. And my hair is now 100 per cent bush."

Nothing in the mangroves is quite what it seems. A log turns out to be a white Humbret, balanced on one leg and politely apologising to the mud. A Whopskip flops onto the deck and announces that it has just jumped a million kilometres before breakfast. It hasn't. A fat Plonkett frog has claimed the anchor and sits on it going plonk, plonk, plonk, as if it's tuning a very small banjo.

Mo serves morning tea: a chocolate mud cake. "Made with real mud," he says proudly. "Local ingredients." Nobody eats it.

"What did the mangrove say to the fog?" asks Mo. "I mist you!"

The groan is so loud and so long that even the Plonkett groans.

Then a tin bathtub glides out of the fog, paddled with a broom by a small woman in round, misted-up glasses. Her yellow raincoat is covered in handwritten poems, a pencil is tucked behind each ear, and a fluffy grey bird with a long, curious neck is nesting on her head.

"Strangers," she says, studying the boat. "Your boat is a soggy sandwich, and you are the filling."

"Was that an insult?" whispers Zed.

"It's a metaphor," says Indi.

"Picture it," says the woman. "I am Poet Pip, and this is Similoon. Be very careful what you compare her to."

"Your bird is as round as a ball," says Mo.

Pop! The Similoon instantly puffs into a perfect fluffy ball, rolls off Pip's head and plops into the water.

Pip fishes her out and dries her on a poem. Then she tells you about Maxx's newest video, "Maxx Braves the Wild Mangroves!" In it, Maxx wades waist-deep through a dark, dangerous swamp, swatting away vines, to rescue a trembling Likkaby. It has fifteen million views.

"His swamp is a painting," says Pip. "His fog is a liar. His mangroves wear price tags."

Everyone looks blank, except Indi, who is an artist and thinks in pictures anyway. "She means the swamp in his video isn't a real swamp at all!"

"Picture it," says Pip, and she points a long, inky finger.

Through a gap in the fog stands a wall of glowing green, as tall as a house and twice as wide. Gold pipes run along the top, puffing out thick clouds of fog that drift lazily across the mangroves. A sign hangs at the front: "GREEN SCREEN SWAMP. CLOSED SET. 100% REAL WILD SWAMP."

"So some of this fog is fake," says Gus, sniffing the air. "It smells like strawberry."

Plonketts are sitting all over the pipes, plonking cheerfully.

"He won't like that," says Wren. "He's scared stiff of frogs."

"Will you help us?" you ask Pip.

"Trust is a seed, Captain," says Pip. "It grows slowly, and only in good soil. Win my badge, and then we shall see what blooms."

Just then, the Similoon unfolds her long neck, flutters off Pip's head and drifts towards the green glow, curious as a kitten.

A voice floats out of the fog. It's Maxx, talking to a camera even though it's nearly dark.

"Whoa. A bird that turns into anything it's compared to? That's Maxx-imum content, Vantafam! Smash that heart button! Somebody bag it!"

A net swishes. The Similoon doesn't come back.

For the first time since you met her, Poet Pip doesn't speak in pictures. Her voice is small and plain.

"They took my bird."
